subject: Copywriting
subcategory: The Science of Storytelling in Ads
title: Always: Like a Girl
description: A quick, practical guide to Always: Like a Girl.

hook.text: The Always #LikeAGirl campaign asked girls to 'run like a girl.' Young girls ran hard. Older girls ran daintily.

buildup.text: The 2014 campaign turned an insult into a battle cry. 'Like a girl' was reframed as fierce, not weak.

discovery.text: It won the Grand Prix at Cannes, an Emmy, and a Grand Clio. It also increased purchase intent by 50%.

twist.text: A feminine hygiene brand rarely generates cultural conversation.

climax.text: #LikeAGirl proved that purpose-driven storytelling sells products AND changes culture. Both outcomes are possible.

punchline.text: An insult became a movement. Story-copy changed the culture.

quiz.question: How much did #LikeAGirl increase purchase intent?

details.summary: Always's 'Like a Girl' campaign challenged the cultural insult by showing that young girls run, throw, and fight 'like a girl' with full power — it's only older people who turn the phrase into mockery. The campaign went viral, won every major advertising award, and repositioned a mundane brand...
details.whyItMatters: Like a Girl demonstrates how brands can create cultural movements through storytelling. By challenging an existing cultural narrative, Always created emotional resonance that transcended its product category entirely.
takeaways: Challenging cultural assumptions creates powerful emotional engagement
The campaign generated 85 million YouTube views and became a cultural touchstone
Purpose-driven storytelling builds brand loyalty that transcends product features

faq.question: Why was Like a Girl so much more successful than typical brand ads?
faq.answer: It didn't sell a product — it championed a cause. By challenging a cultural insult, it tapped into deep emotions around gender identity, self-esteem, and social justice. People shared it as a statement of their values, giving the brand organic reach no media budget could buy.

faq.question: Can purpose-driven storytelling work for any brand?
faq.answer: Only if the purpose is authentic and connected to the brand's actual identity. Always's connection to girls' confidence during puberty was genuine. Brands that adopt causes without authentic connection are quickly called out for performative activism, which damages rather than builds trust.
